questions.q: Simplify $\log_2 8+\log_2 4$ to a single number.
Express $2\ln x-\ln(x-1)$ as a single logarithm.
Simplify $\log_3 54-\log_3 2$ to a single number.
Solve $5^x=20$, giving your answer to three decimal places.
Solve $3^{2x-1}=10$, to three decimal places.
Solve $7^{3x}=50$, to three decimal places.
Solve $\ln(2x-1)=3$, to three decimal places.
Solve $\log_2(x+3)+\log_2(x-1)=5$, rejecting any value outside the domain.
questions.answer: $\log_2\left[(x+3)(x-1)\right]=5\Rightarrow(x+3)(x-1)=32\Rightarrow x^2+2x-3=32\Rightarrow x^2+2x-35=0\Rightarrow(x+7)(x-5)=0$. Domain requires $x>1$, so $x=-7$ is rejected. Solution: $x=5$.

questions.q: Solve $\ln x+\ln(x+3)=\ln10$, rejecting any value outside the domain.
questions.answer: $\ln\left[x(x+3)\right]=\ln10\Rightarrow x(x+3)=10\Rightarrow x^2+3x-10=0\Rightarrow(x+5)(x-2)=0$. Domain requires $x>0$, so $x=-5$ is rejected. Solution: $x=2$.

sections.heading: Properties of the exponential and natural log functions

questions.q: Simplify $e^{\ln7}$ and $\ln(e^4)$, using the fact that $e^x$ and $\ln x$ are inverse functions.
questions.answer: $e^{\ln7}=7$ and $\ln(e^4)=4$, since $e^x$ and $\ln x$ undo each other.

questions.q: Solve $e^{2x}=15$, to three decimal places.

sections.heading: Graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions

questions.q: The graph shows $y=e^x$ and $y=\ln x$. State how the two curves are related geometrically, and state the equation of the asymptote of each.
questions.answer: The two curves are reflections of each other in the line $y=x$, since $y=\ln x$ is the inverse function of $y=e^x$. The asymptote of $y=e^x$ is $y=0$ (the $x$-axis); the asymptote of $y=\ln x$ is $x=0$ (the $y$-axis).

questions.q: The graph shows $y=\ln(x-2)$. State its domain and the equation of its vertical asymptote.
questions.answer: The domain is $x>2$ (the argument $x-2$ must be positive). The vertical asymptote is $x=2$.

sections.heading: Simultaneous equations involving exponentials and logarithms

questions.q: Solve simultaneously $\log_2x+\log_2y=5$ and $x-y=4$, for $x,y>0$.
questions.answer: From the first equation, $xy=2^5=32$. Substituting $x=y+4$: $(y+4)y=32\Rightarrow y^2+4y-32=0\Rightarrow(y+8)(y-4)=0$. Since $y>0$, $y=4$, giving $x=8$.

questions.q: Solve simultaneously $\ln x-\ln y=1$ and $x+y=11$, giving $x$ and $y$ to three decimal places.
questions.answer: From the first equation, $\ln\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)=1\Rightarrow x=ey$. Substituting: $ey+y=11\Rightarrow y(e+1)=11\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{11}{e+1}\approx\dfrac{11}{3.718282}\approx2.958$. Then $x=11-y\approx8.042$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\log_5 30$ using the change of base formula, to three decimal places.
Solve $2^x=3^{x-1}$ using logarithms, to three decimal places.
questions.answer: Take $\ln$ of both sides: $x\ln2=(x-1)\ln3\Rightarrow x\ln2-x\ln3=-\ln3\Rightarrow x(\ln2-\ln3)=-\ln3\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\ln3}{\ln3-\ln2}=\dfrac{1.098612}{0.405465}\approx2.710$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\log_7 3\times\log_3 7$ without a calculator, explaining why the product is exactly 1.
questions.answer: By the change of base formula, $\log_7 3=\dfrac{\ln3}{\ln7}$ and $\log_3 7=\dfrac{\ln7}{\ln3}$. Their product is $\dfrac{\ln3}{\ln7}\times\dfrac{\ln7}{\ln3}=1$, since the $\ln3$ and $\ln7$ factors cancel completely — this holds for any pair of reciprocal-base logarithms $\log_ab\times\log_ba$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: radioactive decay

questions.q: This question has three parts. A radioactive isotope decays according to $A(t)=A_0e^{-kt}$, where $A_0$ is the initial mass (grams) and $t$ is time in years. (a) Given that the isotope has a half-life of 12 years, find the decay constant $k$, to four decimal places. (b) A sample starts with $A_0=80$ grams. Find the mass remaining after 30 years, to two decimal places. (c) Find how long it takes the sample to decay to 5 grams.
questions.answer: (a) $\dfrac{A_0}{2}=A_0e^{-12k}\Rightarrow e^{-12k}=0.5\Rightarrow-12k=\ln0.5\approx-0.693147\Rightarrow k\approx0.0578$. (b) $A(30)=80e^{-0.0578(30)}=80e^{-1.7329}\approx80(0.1768)\approx14.14$ grams. (c) Solve $80e^{-0.0578t}=5\Rightarrow e^{-0.0578t}=\dfrac{5}{80}=\dfrac{1}{16}$. Since $\dfrac{1}{16}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4$, this corresponds to exactly $4$ half-lives, so $t=4\times12=48$ years.
